In the passage, Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, is a significant figure in Jewish history who led the Jews back from Babylon around 520 BC, governed Judah, and rebuilt the temple. The Old Testament records several instances where he is called a son of Shealtiel.

In the Book of Chronicles, Zerubbabel's descendants are traced for several generations, and at times 1, 2, ..., k+i–1, observations are made to estimate a forecasting model. The error on the forecast for k+i is then computed. This process is repeated for i = 2,...,T–k, where T is the total number of observations. The forecast accuracy is determined by evaluating all errors computed. This procedure is often referred to as a "rolling forecasting origin" because the "origin" (k+i -1) at which the forecast is based moves forward in time.

Two-step-ahead or, in general, p-step-ahead forecasts can be computed by first following the above-mentioned steps to generate a forecast for the next p time periods. This process can be repeated for various values of p to evaluate the accuracy of the forecasts over different time horizons.
